questions.text: When customers use your product or service for its core purpose, is there evidence it achieves the outcome they need?

A.text: No evidence gathered on whether the outcome is achieved

B.text: Anecdotal impressions suggest it helps; nothing observed or measured systematically

C.text: Direct observation or structured feedback confirms the outcome is achieved in typical cases

D.text: Confirmed across a range of customers and use cases, not only typical or best-case ones

E.text: Confirmed and measured on an ongoing basis, so degradation or edge-case failure would be caught

questions.text: How consistently does your product or service perform without defects, failures, or errors that affect the customer?

A.text: Not tracked, or failures are the norm rather than the exception

B.text: Tracked informally; recurring issues still require individual fixes

C.text: Tracked with some consistency; most instances are caught and resolved, though not systematically prevented

D.text: Tracked systematically; failures are the exception rather than a recurring pattern

E.text: Tested systematically across realistic use cases, failures are the exception, and a defined process exists for detecting and correcting them before broader release

questions.text: Does your product or service cover what is necessary for the customer's core need, or are there gaps that force workarounds?

A.text: Significant gaps force reliance on manual workarounds or other providers for essential parts of the core need

B.text: Some gaps exist; customers manage them but have raised them as real friction

C.text: The core need is covered; known gaps concern adjacent or secondary needs

D.text: The core need is covered with no material gaps, confirmed by customer feedback rather than internal assumption

E.text: Core need fully covered, with necessary components tested against realistic target use cases and no material gaps identified

questions.text: How does the business collect and act on feedback about how the product or service performs?

A.text: No systematic collection; issues surface only if a customer complains

B.text: Collected informally and inconsistently; no clear process for acting on it

C.text: Collected with some consistency; some of it visibly leads to changes

D.text: Collected through a defined channel or process, with a consistent pattern of acting on it

E.text: Systematic collection with specific changes the business can point to, made because of it, on an ongoing basis

questions.text: Is your product or service delivered through a standardised process that can be repeated without disproportionate manual or specialist effort each time?

A.text: Every delivery requires substantial bespoke, non-repeatable effort — the founder or a specialist is required each time

B.text: Some parts are repeatable, but delivery still depends heavily on specific individuals or ad hoc effort

C.text: Core delivery is systematised — documented, templated, or productised — though exceptions still require significant bespoke work

D.text: Core delivery is systematised and bespoke handling is the exception; most delivery goes through the standard process

E.text: Fully systematised and documented so another appropriately skilled person could execute the standard process without relying on the founder's undocumented knowledge; tested in a realistic pilot or simulation
